summary: Narrow verification of revision 8 edits to the knee-edge OOD draft, focused on the K1a gap floor and the minus-infinity anchor convention; skeptic; readiness critic

packed.verdict: The r8 gate logic is mostly sound, but it is not yet clean enough for A1. One more text-only pass is needed; the accepted design does not change. Gap floor (ii) closes the round-7 loophole as round 7 stated it: a negative median RANDOM KC can no longer lower the required median CUTOFF gap, and the 0.37 case is now blocked. With the minus-infinity convention, per-anchor dominance holds for the median of differences in K1a (i), for (ii), and for K1c's absolute clause. I re-derived all the arithmetic: 0.016/0.20/0.40, 0.72-1.07, about 0.97 vs about 1.07 at w = 0.05, the 0.51 check behind the 0.37 example, and 0.34. The tolerance directions are correct and worded the same way in Part 2, V0(b), Part 8.2 and Review 8 row 4. The A3 flag text is wired in. Several of the new claims are still stronger than the logic supports. (1) 'A K1a miss driven by RANDOM is then INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL' is false: if the gate passes with a positive KC_R inside V0(b)'s band, a CUTOFF critic that over-values by 0.7 gets labelled FAIL. Reading 2's guard only withholds the reading. (2) Floor (ii) works on medians, not per anchor, so a K1a PASS can still rest on low-gap anchors where RANDOM was pessimistic. The text claims otherwise, and the residual round 7 recorded is not disclosed. (3) The dominance claim does not cover K1c's relative clause, which uses a mixed anchor set. (4) The step 0.4 partial-forecast claims ignore the new minus-infinity convention, use 'only if' where 'if' is meant, and bound |KC_R| where only positive KC_R matters. (5) The joint tolerance silently assumes rho_R = rho_C. (6) The A4 prediction appears only in Part 2 and is not wired into the Part 5 step 0.4 PASS row or the Stage 1 (A4) section. Items 1 and 2 are medium because they misstate what a label means. The rest are wording, disclosure or bookkeeping fixes.

low_findings.section: Part 2 Pessimistic anchors (:206); Anchor sets (:634); K1c row (:664); Review 8 row 3 (:1038)
low_findings.claim: 'Per-anchor dominance carries over: if the gate passes, a smooth CUTOFF critic passes the criterion' holds for K1a (i), for (ii) and for K1c's ABSOLUTE clause. It does not hold for K1c's RELATIVE clause. That clause compares a median of KC_s10 over the COMMON anchors, where a non-C-valid anchor has unknown smooth KC, with 0.5 x a median of rho_hat_C over the C-valid anchors only. The minus-infinity entries move the gate's median down to about the 44th percentile of the C-valid values, while the relative bar uses the C-valid median.
low_findings.evidence: 48 common anchors: 5 non-C-valid (just under item 5's 10%) with smooth KC of about 0, 21 at rho_hat_C(s10) = 0.66 and 22 at 1.4. K1c gate median = 0.66 >= 0.65, so it passes. With exact smooth KC = rho_hat, median KC_s10 over the common anchors = 0.66, below the relative bar 0.5 x 1.4 = 0.70, so the clause fails. Even at the lower tolerance end, the absolute clause gives 0.51 and passes while the relative clause fails (ex.py case C). Without the set mismatch, the relative clause follows from the gate (M - 0.15 >= 0.5M whenever M >= 0.3).
low_findings.fix: Either take K1c's relative-clause median over the same set as the KC median, with the same minus-infinity convention, or restrict the dominance sentence to 'K1a and K1c's absolute clause' and say the relative clause is not covered.

low_findings.claim: The partial-forecast statements were not updated for r8's own minus-infinity convention, and the logical connective points the wrong way. (a) 'Implies K1c's reachability and K1a's gap floor ... because items 1 and 2 have medians of at least 0.75' fails once up to 10% of anchors enter as minus infinity. Step 0.4's items are medians over predictor-valid anchors, while the gate's median is over common anchors with minus-infinity entries, so it can fall to about the 44th percentile. (b) 'Implies K1a's contrast term only if |KC_R| <= 0.15 at every anchor' states a necessary condition, but the bound is sufficient and not necessary, so it should read 'if'. Only positive KC_R matters, so the condition is KC_R <= 0.15, not |KC_R| <= 0.15. It is also sufficient only when no anchor enters as minus infinity. (c) 'V0(b) admits up to about 0.34' holds only at median rho_hat_R = 0.75 (0.4 x 0.85), and V0(b) bounds the median KC_R, not each anchor.
low_findings.evidence: Items 1-2 at :184-186 use medians over predictor-valid anchors. Bimodal example: 44 valid anchors, 22 at 0.55 and 22 at 0.95 at s10 (median 0.75, item 2 passes), plus 4 minus-infinity entries; the gate median is 0.55 < 0.65. At s05, 22 at 0.45 and 22 at 1.05 (median 0.75, item 1 passes), and gate (ii) = 0.35 < 0.5. Sufficiency check: median[rho_hat - 0.25] >= 0.75 - 0.25 = 0.5 only when every entry is finite. 0.4 x (0.75 + 0.10) = 0.34.
low_findings.fix: Write: 'implies K1c's reachability and K1a's gap floor if every anchor is C-valid and approximately otherwise; it implies K1a's contrast term if, in addition, KC_s05,R <= 0.15 at every anchor (a sufficient condition, not a necessary one); V0(b) admits a median |KC_R| of up to about 0.34 at median rho_hat_R = 0.75.'

low_findings.claim: The tolerated ratio KC_R/rho = (rho - 0.6)/rho silently assumes rho_R = rho_C, the same unstated equal-rho assumption that round 7 item 7 flagged for the worst-case figure. Clause (i) bounds KC_R in absolute terms (KC_R <= rho_hat_C - 0.6), while the softplus ratio scales KC_R with RANDOM's own rho_R. When rho_R > rho_C, which is plausible because a less competent RANDOM continuation gives larger state magnitudes, the same rounding width costs more than the table suggests. 'At the typical anchor' also hides that (i) is a median of differences.
low_findings.evidence: (0.61 - 0.6)/0.61 = 0.0164, 0.15/0.75 = 0.20, 0.4/1.0 = 0.40, all correct at equal rho. Ratio 0.25 (w = 0.02) with rho_C = 0.75: the bound KC_R <= 0.15 holds when rho_R = 0.5 (0.125) but fails when rho_R = 1.2 (0.30). Old actors gave rho 1.13-1.45 (:194).
low_findings.fix: State the assumption: 'with rho_R = rho_C; in general, (i) needs ratio_R x rho_R <= rho_hat_C - 0.6 at the typical anchor.' Mirror the change in Part 8.2(iii).

low_findings.section: Part 5 step 0.4 label table (:589); Stage 1 (approval A4) (:592ff); Part 8.2 (:833)
low_findings.claim: The standing written prediction 'Stage 1 V0(d) may end INCONCLUSIVE', acknowledged at A4, appears only in Part 2 (:202). Part 5, which governs approvals, does not carry it. The step 0.4 PASS row says only 'It permits only the request for Stage 1', and the Stage 1 (approval A4) section never mentions it. Part 8.2's 'current forecast is borderline' bullet does not refer to the A4 acknowledgement either. By contrast, the step 0.3 flag text 'V0(b) or V0(d)' is correctly wired into the A3 consequence (:563).
low_findings.evidence: grep 'A4' finds the acknowledgement only at :202 and :1041. :589 reads 'PASS. It permits only the request for Stage 1'. :592-599 have no prediction text.
low_findings.fix: In the step 0.4 PASS row (or the Stage 1 header), add: 'The A4 request carries the standing written prediction "Stage 1 V0(d) may end INCONCLUSIVE" (LQR proxy rho(s05) about 0.61 against about 0.6 + positive KC_R), acknowledged by the user at A4.' Cross-reference it from Part 8.2.

low_findings.claim: 'So a smooth critic certainly clears their bars' overstates. The premise at :204 is approximate ('KC ... of about the true rho'), so the clearance is only as exact as that approximation. Any additive KC noise or target-smoothing contamination of the -KNEE reference (Part 8.5) in CUTOFF's own critic can push a 'correct' critic below rho_hat - tol. This is the same power cost already disclosed for RANDOM in 8.2(iii), here on the CUTOFF side.
low_findings.evidence: :204 'has KC at a slot of about the *true* rho'; :205 'certainly clears'; Part 8.5 (:857) says KC differencing assumes the contamination cancels.
low_findings.fix: Replace 'certainly' with 'clears up to its own KC noise', and add CUTOFF-side KC noise to 8.2(iii) as a power cost.

low_findings.claim: The revision-8 note says rows 2, 4, 5 and 8 were refined. Review 7 row 9 ('4.8 builds slots with the builder and asserts equality with the saved actions') was also superseded by r8 item 2 (slots 1-5 only; slot 0 by forward pass), but the note does not flag it. Row 9 now states a check that fails by construction.
low_findings.evidence: :1024 row 9 compared with :452-454 and Review 8 row 2 (:1037). The note at :1027 lists 'Rows 2, 4, 5 and 8'.
low_findings.fix: Add row 9 to the r8 refinement note: '4.8 compares slots 1-5 only; slot 0 is reproduced by a forward pass'.

verified.section: Part 2 Link to Stage 1, K1a (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:211); V0(d) rationale (:655-656); Review 8 row 1 (:1036)
verified.claim: 'A K1a miss driven by RANDOM is then INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL' is false as the precedence is written. Gate (i) only guarantees that a fully smooth CUTOFF critic (KC_C,j >= rho_hat_C,j - 0.10) would pass. When the gate passes, a CUTOFF critic that over-values strongly but a bit less than its rho, together with a positive KC_R inside V0(b)'s band, gives a K1a miss that is caused by RANDOM, and the label is FAIL. Under 5.0 precedence, INCONCLUSIVE comes only from a V0 item, and V0(d) passes in this case.
verified.evidence: Uniform 48 anchors: rho_hat_C(s05) = 0.9, KC_R = 0.3, KC_C = 0.7. Gate (i) median[0.9 - 0.10 - 0.3] = 0.50, so it passes. (ii) 0.80 passes. V0(b): |0.3| <= 0.4 x (0.9 + 0.10) = 0.40, so it passes. K1a = 0.7 - 0.3 = 0.40, a FAIL. With an exact RANDOM, K1a would be 0.70, a PASS. Reading 2's guard (0.3 > 0.1 x 0.9 = 0.09) only withholds the mechanistic reading (:687). The label is still FAIL, and 'Every FAIL stops the plan' (:495). Script at C:\Users\David\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-David-dev-BCA\be215736-77cd-47c3-bb51-9f394d41a6ce\scratchpad\verify_wf_r8\gate_logic\ex.py, case B.
verified.fix: Restate :211 precisely: 'A K1a miss that a smoothly extrapolating CUTOFF critic would suffer because of RANDOM's KC is INCONCLUSIVE. When the gate passes, a K1a miss means CUTOFF fell below rho_hat_C - 0.10 at enough anchors; RANDOM's positive KC can still contribute, and then the label is FAIL with no reading (reading 2's guard).' Disclose this FAIL path in Part 8.2(iii). Optionally, but only with the user's sign-off since it changes labels, make a K1a miss INCONCLUSIVE whenever reading 2's guard fails.

check.reason: The arithmetic holds. With rho_hat_C = 0.9, KC_R = 0.3 and KC_C = 0.7 at all anchors, gate (i) gives 0.50 and passes, (ii) gives 0.80 and passes, and V0(b)'s allowance 0.4 x (0.9 + 0.10) = 0.40 admits KC_R = 0.3. K1a is then 0.40, a FAIL; with an exact RANDOM it would be 0.70, a PASS. Under 5.0's precedence (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:488-495) the label is FAIL, and only reading 2's guard at :687 is withheld. So the sentence at :211, 'A K1a miss driven by RANDOM is then INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL', is broader than the rule. It holds only for a CUTOFF critic that clears rho_hat_C - 0.10 at enough anchors, which is the rationale at :206 and :655. Nothing else in the draft corrects this. Part 8.2(iii) (:832-836) discloses only the INCONCLUSIVE masking path and says 'costs power, not validity', not this FAIL path. Severity is low, not medium. The FAIL label is consistent with 5.0's definitions and with V0(b) accepting RANDOM's rounding as a valid control. This case needs CUTOFF to under-represent its own gap, KC_C 0.7 against a true rho of at least 0.8, so the miss is joint, not caused by RANDOM alone. Making it INCONCLUSIVE would contradict the settled observed-RANDOM form. The fix is wording plus a disclosure line in 8.2(iii); changing labels would need the user's sign-off, as the finding itself says. The sentence originated in the r7 critic's recommended text (VERIFY_CRITIC_DIGEST_r7.txt item 1 FIX), so it carried over rather than being introduced as a logic change.

verified.claim: Gap floor (ii) is a floor on a median, not a per-anchor floor. 'A negative RANDOM KC never lowers the gap required' and 'Clause (ii) keeps this true whatever the sign of RANDOM's KC' therefore hold only for the median gap. K1a is a median of DIFFERENCES. Its upper half can be made up almost entirely of anchors where CUTOFF's gap is small and RANDOM is pessimistic, while V0(b), which bounds only the median KC_R, and both gate clauses still pass. A K1a PASS is then attributed to withholding at anchors whose true CUTOFF gap is about 0.25-0.35. The residual that the round-7 critic recorded ('the K1a contrast itself can be inflated by RANDOM under-valuing the onset') is not disclosed anywhere in r8.
verified.evidence: n = 49 anchors. 24 anchors have rho_hat_C = 0.25 and KC_R = -0.45. 25 anchors have rho_hat_C = 0.70, with KC_R = 0 at one and +0.45 at 24. Gate (i): median = 0.60, passes. (ii): median 0.60, passes. V0(b): median KC_R = 0, passes. K1a with a smooth CUTOFF (KC_C = rho_hat) is 0.70, a PASS. 96% of the anchors at or above K1a's median have rho_hat_C < 0.6 (ex.py case A49). There are no hits for 'inflat' or a similar disclosure in DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md.
verified.fix: Qualify :211 and :655 to say 'never lowers the required median gap'. Add the anchor-level residual to Part 8.2: K1a's margin can come from RANDOM pessimism at low-gap anchors. Optionally report, not gate, two numbers: the share of K1a's upper-half anchors with rho_hat_C - 0.10 < 0.5, and median KC_s05(CUTOFF) by itself as a RANDOM-independent companion to K1a.

check.reason: Refuted in part. The wording at :211 ('never lowers the gap required') and at :655 ('Clause (ii) keeps this true whatever the sign') concerns the reachability gate, and for the gate it is accurate. Gate (ii) is a median floor that does not depend on RANDOM, and in the n = 49 example the median rho_hat_C is 0.70, so the gate's median-gap requirement is met. The wording itself is therefore not wrong. What does stand is the anchor-level K1a inflation. I reproduced the example: gate (i) and (ii) both give 0.60, the median KC_R is 0, and K1a with a smooth CUTOFF is 0.70, carried by anchors with rho_hat_C = 0.25 and KC_R = -0.45. This is exactly the r7 critic's RESIDUAL bullet ('the K1a contrast itself can be inflated by RANDOM under-valuing the onset'; VERIFY_CRITIC_DIGEST_r7.txt RESIDUAL 2), and r8 does not disclose it: grep finds no hit for inflat, under-valu, or K1a margin in DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md, and Part 8 items 1-10 (:816-858) omit it. Severity is low, not medium. r7 classed it as a residual, not a must-fix. It needs RANDOM pessimism of about 1.8 x rho at low-gap anchors, anti-correlated with CUTOFF's gap, which V0(b) permits only because it bounds the median alone. It affects K1a's attribution only, since K1c's absolute bar and K2/K3 are independent of RANDOM (:661-667). No gate or label rule is wrong. The fix is a one-line Part 8.2 disclosure, plus the optional reported, ungated companion numbers.

checked_ok: Gap floor (ii) closes the round-7 loophole at the median level. With (ii), median[rho_hat_C - 0.10] >= 0.5, the old 0.37 case fails (0.27 < 0.5) for any sign of KC_R. The example arithmetic is correct: V0(b) at rho_hat_R = 0.5 admits 0.4 x 0.6 = 0.24, and 0.37 - 0.10 + 0.24 = 0.51.

Per-anchor dominance with the minus-infinity convention holds for the median of DIFFERENCES in K1a (i). On C-valid anchors, KC_C,j - KC_R,j >= (rho_hat_C,j - 0.10) - KC_R,j. On non-C-valid anchors the gate term is minus infinity, which is below anything. The median is monotone in each coordinate, so gate >= 0.5 implies smooth K1a >= 0.5. The same holds for (ii) and for K1c's absolute clause (rho_hat - 0.15 >= 0.5).

The minus-infinity convention is consistent with item 5's 90% rule: at most 10% of entries are minus infinity, because V0(d) item 5 requires >= 90% C-valid among the common anchors under CUTOFF's continuation. It is also consistent with V0(c)'s floor of >= 32 C-valid. The convention is stated the same way in Part 2 (:206, :215), Part 5 anchor sets (:634), V0(d) (:648-651) and Part 8.2 (:828), and in Part 9 Review 6 row 1 (:992) and Review 8 row 3.
CR-valid is fully removed from the operative text. Its only remaining mentions are historical: Review 7 row 5 (:1019) and the r8 note saying it was dropped (:1027).
Joint tolerance arithmetic, assuming equal rho: (0.61 - 0.6)/0.61 = 0.0164, 0.15/0.75 = 0.20, 0.4/1.0 = 0.40.
Worst-case range: 0.6 + 0.4 x (0.2 + 0.10) = 0.72; at rho_hat_R = rho_hat_C, rho = 0.64/0.6 = 1.067.

w = 0.05 comparison (softplus ratio 0.38, equal rho, the same model as in the round-7 digest): the chosen form needs 0.6/(1 - 0.38) = 0.968, about 0.97, against 1.07 for the worst case; with an exact RANDOM, 0.6 against 1.07.

The partial-forecast bound (with KC_R <= 0.15 at every anchor and no minus-infinity entries) is sufficient: median[rho_hat - 0.25] >= 0.75 - 0.25 = 0.5. 'V0(b) admits up to about 0.34' equals 0.4 x (0.75 + 0.10) at the reference median.

The tolerance direction is correct. rho_hat - rho = min_k P_k - Q_nostall lies in [-tol, tol]. The reachability gates use rho >= rho_hat - tol, and V0(b)'s 0.4 x (rho_hat_R + 0.10) >= 0.4 rho_R, so RANDOM with ratio <= 0.4 is not rejected. The wording matches across Part 2 (:205), the V0(b) coverage bullet (:218) and Review 8 row 4.

V0(d)'s rule 'If either reachability condition fails in any seed, Stage 1 is INCONCLUSIVE' (:652) together with 5.0 precedence (:490-494) correctly makes a gate miss INCONCLUSIVE and voids any observed K1 pass.
Anchor sets are named for V0(b)'s floor and ratio (R-valid), item 5 (common anchors under each continuation), K1c's relative clause (C-valid) and reading 2 (R-valid).
The step 0.3 flagged row carries 'Stage 1 V0(b) or V0(d) may end INCONCLUSIVE', acknowledged at A3 (:563).
Part 8.2's 'Together these need rho_C(s05) of about 0.6, plus any positive RANDOM KC' and the rewording 'a correct critic's pass could not be attributed' are correct.
The narrower 'K1a-only miss voids only K1a' scoping is correctly marked as not adopted without the user's sign-off (:840).

packed.verdict: Revision 8 resolves most of the 11 r7 must-fix items, and the core gate logic is now right. The RANDOM-independent gap floor (ii) closes the negative-KC_R hole: at rho_hat_R = 0.5, KC_R = -0.24 and a CUTOFF gap of 0.37, the floor gives 0.27 < 0.5. The tolerance direction is correct. CR-valid is gone from the body text. The joint-tolerance and worst-case arithmetic reproduces: 0.016 / 0.20 / 0.40, 0.968, 1.067, and 0.72 at rho_hat_R = 0.2. The 4.8 rewrite matches evaluation.py: `fixed_candidate_bank` (lines 57-65) puts the actor's command in slot 0 and FIXED_A0 with zero a1..a3 in slots 1-5, and the saved per_probe actions are (32, 6, 4) with exact zeros in slots 1-5. The reference.py citations are correct, and all 32 Part 11 hashes match, including the three new r7 rows. It is not quite clean, though. First, the 4.4 exemption for slot 0 covers only the a1..a3 zero assertion, not the index-0 slot-value assertion, so the gated 4.8 array still fails a 4.4 assertion by construction. Second, the new minus-infinity convention makes the Part 2 claim that a step 0.4 PASS 'implies K1c's reachability and K1a's gap floor' false when up to 10% of anchors are predictor-invalid, and its quantile cost is not disclosed. Third, the Part 9 notes still leave Review 7 row 9 and Review 6 rows 3 and 6 stale. Everything else is a low citation or wording issue. One more short text-only pass would make r8 ready for A1; no design change is needed.

low_findings.section: Part 2 partial forecast (:198-200) vs Pessimistic anchors (:206); Part 8.2(iii) (:836-840)
low_findings.claim: Under the r8 convention, where non-C-valid anchors enter the reachability medians as minus infinity, 'a step 0.4 PASS implies K1c's reachability and K1a's gap floor' is no longer true. Step 0.4's items 1 and 2 take medians over predictor-valid anchors only, and item 5 lets up to 10% of anchors be invalid. With 10% at minus infinity, each reachability median falls to about the 44th percentile of the valid anchors. That stricter quantile, a power cost, is not disclosed.
low_findings.evidence: Counterexample: 48 gated anchors (step 0.4, :576), 4 invalid (8.3% < 10%, item 5 passes), and 44 valid, of which 23 have rho_hat(s05) = 0.75 and 21 have 0.45. Item 1's median (mean of the 22nd and 23rd values) is 0.75, and >= 0.4 holds at 100%, so step 0.4 passes. The full-set median with 4 x minus infinity is the mean of the 24th and 25th values, 0.45, so the gap floor is 0.35 < 0.5. The same construction at s10 breaks the 'implies K1c reachability' claim. Part 8.2(iii) lists the joint tolerance 'at the typical anchor' but not the quantile shift.
low_findings.fix: Qualify :199: 'implies K1c's reachability and K1a's gap floor when the same minus-infinity convention is applied to step 0.4's medians (report that statistic in step 0.4), or when every gated anchor is predictor-valid'. Better, compute and report step 0.4's forecast with the V0(d) convention. Add one line to 8.2(iii): with k% of anchors non-C-valid, each reachability median sits at about the (50 - k)/(100 - k) quantile of the C-valid values.

low_findings.section: Part 2 Pessimistic anchors (:206); K1c table row (:664)
low_findings.claim: 'If the gate passes, a smooth CUTOFF critic passes the criterion' is too strong for K1c. K1c has a second, relative clause, >= 0.5 x median rho_hat_C(s10) over the C-valid anchors. The reachability gate does not cover it, and it is not implied when rho_hat is skewed across anchors.
low_findings.evidence: The K1c gate (:215, :651) checks only median rho_hat_C(s10) >= 0.65 under the minus-infinity convention, which bounds the smooth critic's median KC by about p44(C-valid rho_hat) - 0.15. The relative clause (:664) needs median KC >= 0.5 x p50(C-valid rho_hat). With p44 = 0.65 and p50 = 2.0, which is plausible because rho scales with |Q| and so with the remaining horizon at t = 0/25/50, the gate passes but the bound gives 0.5 < 1.0.
low_findings.fix: Write 'a smooth CUTOFF critic passes K1a and K1c's absolute clause', or note that the relative clause is not covered by the gate.

low_findings.claim: The tolerances are inconsistent. The slot 0 actor forward pass must match the saved actions 'exactly', while the q1 forward pass on the same float32 networks gets 1e-6 relative. The text also does not say whether the 1e-9 Q^pi reproduction covers slot 0.
low_findings.evidence: The rerun's own pre-registered rule allowed Tier 2 floats within 1e-6*(1+|old|) (evaluate_worker.py:124-125). The realized result was 143/143 Tier-1 exact (run/evaluation/report.json reproduction.tier1_exact = 143), but that was the same code path. The 'new evaluator' may batch or jit differently, and bitwise float32 equality is then not guaranteed, which would give INCOMPLETE with no real fault. q1/twin_min/adjusted are restricted to 'slots 1-5' (:454), but :457 ('saved per-probe Q^pi') names no slot range.

critic.verdict:
Revision 8 is logically sound on the gates and needs one more text-only pass. The design is unchanged. No high item remains. Every remaining item is wording, scoping, disclosure or bookkeeping, and none changes how a gate decides.

RULING ON GAP FLOOR (ii): correct as written. median_j[rho_hat_C,j(s05) - 0.10] >= 0.5 does not depend on RANDOM. It blocks the round-7 case: 0.37 - 0.10 = 0.27 < 0.5 for any sign of KC_R. I re-checked: 0.4 x 0.6 = 0.24 and 0.37 - 0.10 + 0.24 = 0.51. With (ii), a negative median RANDOM KC can no longer lower the median gap the gate requires. One limit is not disclosed. (ii) floors a median, not each anchor. K1a is a median of differences, so a K1a PASS can still be carried by low-gap anchors where RANDOM was pessimistic. In the 49-anchor example, gate (i) and (ii) both give 0.60, the median KC_R is 0, and the smooth K1a is 0.70, driven by anchors with rho_hat_C = 0.25 and KC_R = -0.45. This is the residual that round 7 recorded, and r8 must disclose it. It does not make (ii) wrong.

RULING ON THE MINUS-INFINITY CONVENTION: correct, with one scoping fix. The median is monotone in each coordinate, and on C-valid anchors the gate term is at most the smooth criterion term. So gate pass implies smooth-critic pass for K1a (i), for (ii) and for K1c's ABSOLUTE clause. The convention is consistent with item 5's 90% rule (at most 10% of entries are minus infinity) and with V0(c)'s C-valid floor of 32. It is stated the same way at :206, :634, :648-651, :828 and in Review 8 row 3. 'Valid anchor' (:53) and 'predictor-valid' (:54) are defined, so 'common gated anchors' (:631) is well defined. It does NOT cover K1c's RELATIVE clause (:664), which takes its rho_hat_C median over C-valid anchors only. The sentence at :206, 'if the gate passes, a smooth CUTOFF critic passes the criterion', is therefore too broad. The convention also has an undisclosed power cost: with k% of anchors non-C-valid, each reachability median sits at about the (50 - k)/(100 - k) quantile of the C-valid values, about the 44th percentile at 10%. That cost breaks the Part 2 claim that a step 0.4 PASS 'implies K1c's reachability and K1a's gap floor'.

Arithmetic re-verified (the joint tolerance assumes equal rho): 0.016/0.20/0.40; 0.72-1.07; about 0.97 vs about 1.07 at w = 0.05; 0.34 = 0.4 x 0.85. The tolerance direction (gates use the lower end, V0(b) the upper end) is correct and worded the same everywhere. CR-valid survives only in the Part 9 history rows. The 4.8 slots-1-5 equality matches evaluation.py fixed_candidate_bank (lines 57-65) and the saved (32, 6, 4) arrays. All 32 Part 11 hashes match. A narrower 'K1a-only miss voids only K1a' scoping is noted but correctly not adopted without the user's sign-off.

Refuted or downgraded:
- G8-2's claim that the :211 and :655 wording is wrong: that wording describes the gate's median requirement and is accurate. Only the missing anchor-level disclosure survives.
- R8-1: on a strict reading of 'gated' (:52), its 'fails by construction' claim does not fire. It survives as an internal inconsistency that r8's own :360 edit created. It fails closed (INCOMPLETE), so it is low.
- G8-1 survives as a wording overstatement of what a label means. It is not a gate defect.

residual_risks: The current forecast is borderline. The clipped-LQR proxy puts the expected CUTOFF value gap at about 0.61, against a reachability level of about 0.6 plus any positive RANDOM KC. A competent learner may well end Stage 1 INCONCLUSIVE with no answer, and the user is asked to acknowledge that in writing at A4.

Learner competence: Stage 1 learners keep the system in smaller states than the old actors did, which shrinks the value gap the test needs. The step 0.4 PASS is only a partial forecast of Stage 1 reachability.

RANDOM's own kink rounding and its never-measured KC noise can make K1a unreachable even when RANDOM is a valid control. That costs power, and one seed's miss masks otherwise clean K1c, K2 and K3 outcomes.

The gates control medians, not individual anchors. A K1a PASS can still partly reflect RANDOM under-valuing the onset at anchors where CUTOFF's true gap is small. This needs disclosure; the design does not prevent it.

A K1a FAIL can still partly reflect RANDOM's positive rounding when CUTOFF's critic is not fully smooth. The label stays FAIL with no mechanistic reading, so a FAIL is a joint statement about both critics.

With up to 10% of anchors not C-valid, the minus-infinity convention makes each reachability median act like roughly a 44th-percentile test, which is somewhat stricter than the step 0.4 medians suggest.
K1c's relative clause is not protected by the reachability gate. A correct CUTOFF critic could fail it when the rho values are skewed across anchors and some anchors are not C-valid.
Known-answer reproduction may stop as INCOMPLETE on float-level differences if slot 0 must match exactly under a re-batched evaluator. This fails safe but costs a rerun and a fresh A2.
The narrower 'K1a-only miss voids only K1a' scoping remains an open decision for the user; it is noted in the draft and not adopted.
